precepts.text: Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things. Your eye is connected to your mind, and your mind is connected to your mouth. You see, you entertain, then you begin to talk: let me get your number. Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh. Eye, mind, mouth: no control, and then you're caught up.
precepts.point: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, and guide thine heart in the way: guard your heart and mind in these commandments and laws.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
“Hear thou, my son, and be wise, and guide thine heart in the way”: guard your heart and your mind in these commandments and these laws. Jump down the same chapter and see what happens to the heart that is not guided: “Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.”

Your eyes behold an evil woman, and your heart begins to utter. Does your heart utter anything? You utter from your mouth. So your eye is connected to your mind, and your mind is connected to your mouth. You see, you entertain, and then you begin to talk: hey, let me get your number, what's going on? Now you're talking, and you have no self-control over your members. Eye, mind, mouth. Out of the abundance of your heart your mouth speaks. No control, and then you're caught up.

It is the same road envy travels in verse 17, “Let not thine heart envy sinners”. Young people see the rapper's house, the girls, the car; the eyes instruct the mind, and the mind begins to envy: I want that, I want to be part of that. When you entertain it, you're telling God, that's what I choose, and this book isn't important. That is why we went into captivity: we did not serve the Lord with joyfulness and gladness of heart for the abundance of all things.

So guide thine heart in the way. Turn the eyes away before the mind takes hold and the mouth follows; that is self-control, and it keeps you in the fear of the Lord all the day long.

precepts.text: As a man thinketh in his heart, so is he; the heart is the mind, and what is planted there comes out in how you carry yourself.
precepts.point: Being chosen above all people keeps you out of the affairs of this world, their fashions, their hairstyles, their trends and challenges, and keeping up with the Joneses; you cannot flip-flop with every new wave and still carry the speciality the Most High put on you.

note.label: Deuteronomy 7: A Holy People, Chosen Above All People

precepts.why:
“For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he”. The heart is the mind, and what is planted there comes out in how you carry yourself.

That is why “thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God” should be etched into your children's minds from the moment they begin to read, until it is implanted into their spirit. The mind controls the body: what goes into the mind comes out through the body, so a people that knows it is holy and special above all people walks and carries itself differently.

Being chosen above all people keeps you out of the affairs of this world, their fashions, their hairstyles, their trends and challenges, and keeping up with the Joneses. You cannot flip-flop with every new wave and still carry the speciality the Most High put on you. As you think in your heart, so you are.

precepts.text: The mouth of a strange woman is a deep pit for the man abhorred of the Most High.
precepts.point: A whore is a deep ditch and a strange woman a narrow pit. She lies in wait as for a prey and increases the transgressors among men.

note.label: Proverbs 23: Warnings Against Appetite, Wine, and the Strange Woman

precepts.why:
“For a whore is a deep ditch; and a strange woman is a narrow pit.” She lies in wait as for a prey and increases the transgressors among men.

Solomon said the same a chapter before: “The mouth of strange women is a deep pit: he that is abhorred of the Lord shall fall therein.” The mouth of a strange woman is a deep pit for the man abhorred of the Most High. The deep ditch and the narrow pit are the same pit, and the man who falls in it is the one the Lord abhors.

That is why the father says first, “My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.” The heart given to the father and the eyes on his ways do not fall in that pit.
